title: Writing a novel with Showmob
summary: A future-growth sketch: how linked Showmob pages, series, and existing blocks could hold a novel draft—and what would still need to earn a build.

blocks.eyebrow: Growth sketch · not shipped as a novel tool
blocks.title: A novel as linked Showmob pages
blocks.body: This page is a product sketch, not a claim that Showmob writes novels end-to-end today. The idea is simple: each chapter (or scene pack) is an artifact; the book spine is a series; structure, revision, and paced reveals use blocks you already have. Reader participation and durable collaboration would come later—only if a real draft proves the gap.

blocks.title: Growth sketch, not a finished novel workflow
blocks.body: Nothing on this page adds widgets, schema, or persistence. What works today is ordinary Showmob: published JSON pages, series order, and local exercise/checklist state in the browser. Branching choices that stick, shared annotations, and co-author drafts are not built. Treat every “later” item as optional backlog, not a promise.

nodes.title: Chapter page
nodes.detail: One schemaVersion 1 artifact: prose in text blocks, beats in a timeline, revision passes in a checklist.

nodes.title: Book spine
nodes.detail: A series groups chapter slugs with order numbers. The hub already lists series; readers move chapter to chapter.

nodes.title: Room read
nodes.detail: A slideshow block paces a pitch or cold read without leaving the same page.

nodes.title: Local check-in
nodes.detail: An exercise or checklist lets a reader mark a choice or pass in this browser only—until something durable earns a build.

blocks.heading: What you can do today with current widgets
blocks.caption: Same renderer. Novel-shaped jobs, not new block types.
rows: text (+ hero for the chapter open)
Plain scrolling prose. No chapter-length pagination widget.
Order is manual in JSON. No outline that rewrites series.order for you.
Author-written beats. Not a live arc map tied to chapter progress.
Checks live in this browser. Refresh or another device starts clean.
Paced slides inside the page. Not a shared live room.
Answer resets locally. Nothing is saved to a server or shared with the author.

blocks.heading: A thin first novel draft (today)
items: Write one chapter as a published artifact: hero + text for the scene, timeline for the beats you care about.
Add series { id, title, order } so the next chapter can sit on the same spine.
Put revision passes in a checklist and a short pitch in a slideshow if you need a room read.
Optional: one exercise as a reader check-in (“Whose POV felt strongest?”). Expect local-only answers.
Ship the pages. Do not invent widgets until a real draft hits a wall the current bin cannot cover.

blocks.heading: Arcs in Showmob vocabulary
blocks.body: Screenwriting jargon is optional. On Showmob, structure is blocks and series: a book spine (series.order), beat lists (timeline), who-changes-what notes (checklist or compact-table), and escalating stakes as a short diagram. Keep names plain so a draft stays editable by the author who wrote it.

blocks.heading: Three arc layers you can already sketch

nodes.title: Story arc
nodes.detail: Acts or movements as timeline items on a spine page—or as ordered chapter artifacts in the series.

nodes.title: Character threads
nodes.detail: A checklist or compact-table per major character: want, wound, turn, cost. Update it when a chapter earns a change.

nodes.title: Escalating stakes
nodes.detail: A short diagram: pressure → choice → consequence → harder pressure. Link each node to the chapter slug that delivers it.

items.title: Establish the fault line
items.detail: Chapter 1 page: hero + text. Timeline lists the first irreversible fact.

items.title: Cost becomes visible
items.detail: Middle chapters: each page’s timeline names what the protagonist loses if they stall.

items.title: Choice that cannot be undone
items.detail: One chapter owns the turn. Character-thread checklist updates after that publish.

items.title: Consequence lands
items.detail: Final chapter(s): stakes diagram ends on the bill that was always coming.

items.label: Series order matches the reading order
items.detail: If chapter 7 must come before chapter 6 in the reader’s mind, fix series.order—do not rely on file names.

items.label: Every major turn has a home chapter
items.detail: If a beat only lives in your head, put it on that chapter’s timeline or it will drift.

items.label: Character threads update after publish
items.detail: Want / turn / cost change when the chapter ships, not when you plan to write it.

items.label: Stakes escalate on the page
items.detail: If pressure does not get harder, the diagram is decoration—cut or rewrite the middle.

blocks.heading: Reader participation, Showmob-flavored
blocks.body: The goal is not a social CMS. It is paced reveals, occasional choices, and light contribution that still feel like reading a Showmob page. Today that means local exercise and checklist state. Later means durable choices and soft collaboration—only if a novel draft needs them more than another product would.

columns.name: Today (shipped)
columns.detail: Exercise answers and checklist ticks stay in this browser. Slideshow pacing is per reader, per visit. No shared room, no saved branch, no annotation that reaches the author.

columns.name: Later (not shipped)
columns.detail: Branching choice blocks that persist, room reactions on a slideshow, shared annotations on a passage, and co-author draft handoff. Each would need schema, storage, and a clear thin boundary.

blocks.heading: Example reader check-in (local only)
blocks.prompt: After a chapter, which response should Showmob support first if we stay thin?
options: A full forum under every chapter
A single paced choice or check that resets locally until durability is proven
Live co-editing of the chapter prose in the browser
blocks.explanation: Local exercise and checklist already cover a thin check-in. Forums and live co-editing are other products. Persist a choice only when a real draft shows local state is not enough.
blocks.correctFeedback: Right—stay on the thin check-in until a draft forces persistence.
blocks.wrongFeedback: Heavier social or editing surfaces are out of scope for a growth sketch. Prefer one local check first.

blocks.heading: Widgets and functions that would earn a later build

items.label: Arc-map block — not shipped
items.detail: A structured map of story/character stakes linked to chapter slugs. Today: diagram + timeline + series.

items.label: Chapter outline that syncs series.order — not shipped
items.detail: Drag chapters and rewrite order in one place. Today: edit series.order in each artifact JSON.

items.label: Character card — not shipped
items.detail: Reusable card for want, voice, and thread status across pages. Today: compact-table or checklist copied per need.

items.label: Durable reader choices — not shipped
items.detail: Branching that survives refresh and can be summarized for the author. Today: exercise is local-only.

items.label: Soft collaboration — not shipped
items.detail: Shared annotations, room reactions, co-author draft handoff. Today: git + PR for authors; nothing for readers.

blocks.heading: Parked until a draft proves the gap

columns.name: Reuse first
columns.detail: text, timeline, checklist, slideshow, exercise, series, diagram, and compact-table already cover draft, spine, beats, revision, pitch, and local check-ins.

columns.name: Build only when stuck
columns.detail: Add a widget when a real novel draft cannot say the next true thing with the current bin—and when the new block stays renderer-thin with no side effects in v0.

blocks.title: Stay thin on purpose
blocks.body: Showmob remains linked pages and a shared renderer. Do not grow a novel CMS beside it. Only add widgets when a real novel draft proves the gap, and keep each addition honest in the catalog: shipped vs later, local vs durable.

blocks.heading: Two-minute pitch for a Showmob novel

slides.title: Pages, not a new app
slides.body: Chapters are artifacts. The book is a series. Readers get normal URLs.

slides.title: Structure in the bin you have
slides.body: Timeline for beats, checklist for revision and character threads, diagram for stakes.

slides.title: Participation stays light
slides.body: Local check-ins first. Durable choices and soft collaboration wait for evidence.

slides.title: Earn every new widget
slides.body: If the draft works with today’s blocks, ship the draft. Build later only when stuck.

blocks.heading: Start with one chapter and a spine
blocks.body: Publish one chapter page, attach a series order, and put your beats on a timeline. Use a checklist for revision and an exercise only if you want a local reader check-in. Come back to this sketch when a real draft forces a widget the current bin cannot cover.
